question: If $A=\begin{bmatrix} x & y \\ -y & x \end{bmatrix}$ and $|A|=25$, then $A^{-1}$ is:
explanation:
$A^{-1} = \frac{1}{|A|}\begin{bmatrix} x & -y \\ y & x \end{bmatrix}$, since $|A| = x^2 + y^2 = 25$.
So, $A^{-1}= \frac{1}{25}\begin{bmatrix} x & -y \\ y & x \end{bmatrix}$.
Answer: (A).

options.D: $\frac{1}{25}\begin{bmatrix} x & -y \\ y & x \end{bmatrix}$ (with $x, y$ interchanged on diagonal)
